chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughtered while saying the tasbih (Subhanallah), or the takbir (Allahu Akbar), or the tahlil (La ilaha illa Allah), or praised God Mighty and Majestic. He said: All of these are from the Names of God Mighty and Majestic, and there is no objection to it.

key_terms.أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ: the Names of God — referring to the divine names and attributes, the mention of any of which suffices
key_terms.حَمِدَ: praised (said Alhamdulillah — All praise is due to God) — the tahmid formula
key_terms.ذَبَحَ: ritual slaughter — the Islamic method of slaughtering animals for food, which requires invoking God's name
key_terms.سَبَّحَ: said Subhanallah (Glory be to God) — the tasbih formula of divine glorification
key_terms.كَبَّرَ: said Allahu Akbar (God is the Greatest) — the takbir formula
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: no objection/no harm — a jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.هَلَّلَ: said La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but God) — the tahlil formula

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to say Subhanallah or Allahu Akbar instead of Bismillah when slaughtering an animal?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the permissibility of using various forms of divine remembrance during ritual slaughter, beyond the specific formula 'Bismillah.' The Imam (peace be upon him) ruled that any invocation mentioning Allah — whether tasbih, takbir, tahlil, or tahmid — is valid, since all are among the Names and attributes of God. This ruling reflects the inclusive understanding that the purpose of the naming formula is to invoke God's name, not to adhere strictly to one particular phrase.
